# A3 — HOLLOW UNITS: WHERE THE TEXT IS NOT THE UNIT

*Generated by `scripts/ingest/census/a3-hollow-units.ts`. Read-only.*

## ⚠ The specified instrument finds two of the four cases the brief names

| case | brief's expectation | what the `<15 words` / `>20,000 words` test finds |
|---|---|---|
| `written-answers` | 143 rows, ~306,000 words each | **CAUGHT** — 143 rows, median 367,570, 95.8% over 20k |
| legislation dot leaders | ~178,826 one-word sections | **CAUGHT** — 112,554 sections under 15 words across 6 collections (the 178,826 figure came from reading bodies; a word-count proxy under-counts it) |
| `et-decisions` | 131,654 landing pages, median 18 words | **MISSED** — the landing pages sit at 18 words, ABOVE the 15-word floor. Only 3,150 of 293,399 rows fall under it |
| `building-regs` | 21 rows, ~446 words each | **MISSED** — median 318, min 237, max 1,483. Nothing under 15, nothing over 20,000 |

**A length threshold cannot find either miss.** `et-decisions` fails it by 3 words; `building-regs`
cannot fail it at all, because a 318-word row is a perfectly ordinary-looking section — the defect
is not the size of the number, it is that the number describes the wrong document.

### ⚠⚠ This changes Part F by more than two orders of magnitude

F2 says to re-fetch "the real decisions behind" the 131,650 landing pages. **They are
already held.** 131,147 of 131,650 landing pages have their
real document ingested alongside them (`assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/…​.pdf`, 161,749 rows).
Only **503** have nothing behind them.

So F1 (delete the landing pages) stands, and F2 shrinks from ~131,650 fetches to **503**.

⚠ And F1 is safe on metadata: every one of the 161,749 document rows already carries
its own `sectionTitle` and `itemDate`, so deleting the landing rows loses no case name and no date.

### `building-regs` is the same defect, and it is total

All 21 rows are `https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/…-approved-document-…` — the gov.uk
publication page, not the Approved Document. `sectionTitle` is NULL on all 21. **0% of the actual
Approved Documents are held**, and the collection reports `[100% complete]` against a target of 21.

### ⚠ The URL test alone OVER-FLAGS — every candidate was checked by reading a body

| corpus | verdict | evidence (read out of R2) |
|---|---|---|
| `et-decisions` | **HOLLOW** | 18-word stub: case name + "Read the decision" furniture; the judgment PDF is a separate row |
| `building-regs` | **HOLLOW, 100%** | *"Statutory guidance / Structure: Approved Document A / Building regulation in England covering the structural elements of a building. From: MHCLG…"* — 1,982 chars of page furniture. The Approved Document itself is not held. |
| `hmrc-codes-guidance` | **HOLLOW** | *"Form Agree to a water discount scheme… Get emails about this page / Documents / Use the postal form Ref: LT4WD"* + a link to the form. The form is not held. |
| `quangos-govuk` | **HOLLOW** (of the 61,192 landing rows) | 359 chars: *"This annual report sets out the activities and achievements of the ECITB…"* — the abstract, not the report. |
| `planning-policy` | **FALSE POSITIVE — REAL** | `gov.uk/guidance/tree-preservation-orders…` is 49,999 chars of actual Planning Practice Guidance. gov.uk publishes this one as HTML, so the URL pattern is not evidence here. |
| `parliament-treaties` | **probably REAL** | body carries the scrutiny-register fields (*"Debate scheduled: DebateNotScheduled / Brought to attention: 2021-12-02"*), which IS the unit for a CRaG register. |
| `hmrc-tiins` | CANDIDATE | median 154 words; a real TIIN is longer. Not confirmed either way. |

**So the landing-page test is a candidate detector, not a verdict.** One collection in seven that it
flagged is a false positive. Part B must confirm `hollow_units` by reading a body per collection,
not by URL shape alone — the same discipline the case-law stylesheet finding needed.

## ⚠⚠ AND TWO COLLECTIONS DO NOT CONTAIN THEIR OWN SUBJECT AT ALL

This is beyond hollowness: the label names one thing and the rows are another.

| corpus | label | rows | from the nominal source | what is actually in it |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| `oecd` | "OECD iLibrary (free summaries)" | 505 | **0** | **505 of 505 are gov.uk URLs**; 10 so much as mention "oecd" in the URL. 52 are gov.uk NEWS STORIES, 31 are ministerial SPEECHES — one is *"London 2012 sets new world standard on Olympic legacy"*. |
| `ots-reports` | "Office of Tax Simplification Reports" | 497 | — | all gov.uk (correct — OTS published there), but **≥69 are news stories and speeches, not reports**, e.g. *"Speech by the Financial Secretary to the Treasury… at the Private Equity Seminar"*. |

Both report `[100% complete]`: `oecd` est 505 = compiled 505, `ots-reports` est 497 = compiled 497.
**The self-referential denominator certified a collection that contains none of its nominal content.**
This is the same failure V20 found in `college-of-policing` (*"prior content was unfiltered gov.uk
search junk"*), which was blocked for it. These two were not.

⚠ 41 of 74 collections trip the thresholds, which makes them close to useless as a filter: a
parliamentary per-speech corpus is *expected* to carry short interventions ("Hear, hear."), so
`historic-hansard` at 23.2% under 15 words is normal, not hollow. Length alone cannot separate a
short unit from a missing one. `hollow_units` in Part B should be counted by the landing-page test
and by the dot-leader flag (C7), not by a percentile.
